# Part III: One Analysis, Many Publications {.unnumbered .part}



Where Colombia's tap water is tested, the countryside's is far riskier than the towns'. In
2023, of the rural zones (a municipality's countryside, outside its head town) with a
utility-supplied water-risk score, 28% fell in the high-risk or unfit
bands, against 6% of urban ones. And much rural water has no score at
all: that year, 6\.8 million of the 12\.6 million
people in rural zones lived where the open data hold none.

This part asks which kinds of municipal zone exist, judged by water safety, services and context,
and how infant mortality, exam scores and school dropout differ between those kinds. Each row of
its data is a *zone-year*: one municipality's urban zone (the head town) or rural zone in one year.
The analysis groups those rows, so a municipality's two zones can be different kinds. You are the
analyst. Your readers are officials, who need a report, and a municipal council, which needs
slides, and both deserve an answer that says plainly what the data cannot show:

- @sec-water-question pins down what is asked, what the data mean and what the assistant may not do.
- @sec-explore finds where the data are empty or misleading, and meets Tunja, the municipality this
  part follows.
- @sec-prepare turns the table into features a clustering can use, and counts the cost.
- @sec-cluster lets an algorithm group the zone-years, and decides how many groups there are.
- @sec-interpret names the kinds and compares their outcomes.
- @sec-causation asks whether worse water goes with more infant deaths, and why that is not a cause.
- @sec-publish-many turns one set of results into a report, slides, a blog post and a website.

The exercises at the end of the part test whether you can do it without the prompts.

![Where we are: Part III.](media/roadmaps/part-3){.on-light fig-alt="Where we are: Part III, One Analysis, Many Publications, highlighted among the book's three parts. Its chapters: 8, The Question, the Data and the Rules, where you set up the project folder, its data and rules; 9, Look Before You Model, where you build explore.qmd, ending at checkpoint 05; 10, From Table to Features, prepare() and nine comparable features, checkpoint 06; 11, Finding Kinds of Places: k-Means, k-means and the clusters page, checkpoint 07; 12, Interpreting Clusters, named clusters and their outcomes, checkpoint 08; 13, Correlation Is Not Causation, the within-cluster check, checkpoint 09; 14, Publish Many, the report, slides, website and blog, checkpoints 10 to 13; then the exercises for Part III."}
